I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is still the steadiest way for me to make use of the full year, match the local climate, and avoid taking on too much market and management risk at my age. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the ground, so I will carry that through to harvest with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations at the key stages, and only necessary pest and disease sprays. After wheat harvest, I will sow summer maize right away, because it fits the heat and rainfall of our area and gives me a reliable second crop. I will not spread myself across too many crops. I would rather manage two familiar crops well, keep labor organized, control water use, and aim for stable yield instead of chasing something more complicated.
